evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.95, the single horizontal reaction arrow labelled 'r H'. SHARED SUBSTRATE: Equations 8.92-8.95 are four competing decompositions of ONE AND THE SAME even-electron (EE+) ion. The figure block draws that ion's parent at its left edge -- the OE+. molecular ion R'(CH2)3CH(R)-Y(+.)-(CH2)3R" with '+.' printed on Y -- and four reaction arrows labelled 'alpha' fanning out from it, one into each numbered equation. The parent carries 2 drawn fishhooks (one leaving the C-R sigma bond, one leaving the '+.' odd electron on Y, both converging on the forming C=Y(+) pi bond); the third, homolysis hook that releases R. is NOT drawn, R. is simply implied by the 'alpha' label. That alpha-cleavage is an unnumbered preamble shared by all four equations and is NOT encoded in this record, which covers only the numbered 'r H' arrow. INSTANTIATION (convention F): the scheme is generic in Y, R, R' and R"; this record uses Y = O, R' = CH3, R" = CH3 (and R = CH3 for the un-encoded parent), so the EE+ ion is the oxocarbenium CH3(CH2)3CH=O(+)-(CH2)3CH3 (C9H19O+, curator-computed monoisotopic m/z 143.1430; it would arise by loss of CH3. from butyl hexan-2-yl ether, M+. m/z 158.1665). Y = O is the assignment the drawing forces: Y carries exactly three bonds both before (=CH plus one alkyl) and after the reaction, with no fourth substituent drawn; the nitrogen case quoted in the running text (CH2=N(+)RCH2CH2CD2CH3, Equation 8.93) would require that extra substituent. NO m/z and NO intensity is printed anywhere on page 205, so every mass in this record is curator-computed, every species is detected=false and the peak status is 'inferred' (convention F). REACTION AS DRAWN: the mirror image of 8.94. The H-receptor site is now the sp2 CARBON (drawn 'CH=Y(+)(CH2)3R"') and the ring bond running into it is the C-C SINGLE bond to the abbreviated donor chain 'R'-(C3H5)', so that C-C bond is the one that must be cleaved (p. 205: 'With only a single bond at this site (8.94 and 8.95), cleavage of this bond is required'). As in 8.94 the donor chain is drawn as a box with one H written out and no definite ring size; the text's ~30% alpha / ~20% beta / ~50% gamma H-site distribution applies. CURATOR CHOICE: the beta-H route is instantiated for the same reason as in 8.94 (the four drawn arcs form two new bonds, and the new pi bond can only join adjacent carbons), giving the four-membered transition state C1...C3-C4...H. Products: R'-C3H5 (here 1-butene, C4H8, 56.0626) and CH2=Y(+)-(CH2)3R" (here CH2=O(+)-(CH2)3CH3, C5H11O+, 87.0804); the sp2 carbon C1 picks up the hydrogen and becomes the methylene of the product oxocarbenium. ARC COUNT: the book draws 4 arc(s), all single-barb fishhooks, in the same two-converging-pairs layout as 8.94: the upper pair (one hook off the C4-H bond, one hook off the C1-C3 bond) converges on the H...C1 gap = the forming H-C1 bond; the lower pair (one hook off each of the same two bonds) converges inside the (C3H5) box = the forming C3=C4 pi bond. ENCODING LIMITATION: RDKit folds an atom-mapped explicit hydrogen back into its heavy atom's implicit-H count, so the migrating H cannot carry an atom map and every drawn hook that touches it is untranscribable as an ElectronMove. The moves below therefore re-express the drawn hooks at heavy-atom level; the H transfer itself is folded into the implicit-H counts of the two mapped atoms it moves between. Only one of the four hooks avoids the H: move <1> = C1-C3 -> C3-C4, transcribed verbatim. Move <2> repeats those endpoints and is NOT a fifth arc: it is the re-decomposition standing in for the three untranscribable hooks (C4-H -> H-C1, C4-H -> C3=C4, C1-C3 -> H-C1). Heavy-atom bookkeeping is identical to the drawing (C1-C3 -2e, C3-C4 +2e); the H transfer is folded into the implicit-H counts (C4: CH2 -> =CH, C1: CH -> CH2).

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.92, 8.93, 8.94 or 8.95 -- the Chapter 8 index stops at 8.14 -- so NO MØD rule is cross-linked to this record and none is asserted to match. Candidate families were read out of rule_index.json and checked against their DFS before being REJECTED: every hTransition_* rule (e.g. hTransition_unsaturated '[H]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]5{=}[_A+.]6>>[C.]2[C]3[C]4[C]5{=}[_A+]6[H]1', hTransition_saturated_1/_3/_4, esterMcLafferty_rH, h2Transiton_1) starts from an ODD-electron site -- a heteroatom radical cation [_A+.] or a distonic [C.] radical -- and produces a carbon radical, whereas the ion reacting here is a closed-shell EE+ oxocarbenium and no radical exists at any point. The only indexed rules that do act on an EE+ oxocarbenium are the Field-rule pair IMS_8_11 (eq. 8.11) and IMS_8_13 (eq. 8.13), which are the mechanistic analogue of Equation 8.94 (H to the heteroatom + cleavage of the Y-C single bond + alkene expulsion). Two findings from checking them: (i) SCOPE -- IMS_8_11 '[C]1([H]2)([H]3)([H]4)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)[O+]8{=}[C]9([H]10)([H]11)>>[C]1([H]2)([H]3)[C]5([H]6)([H]7).[H]4[O+]8{=}[C]9([H]10)([H]11)' requires a terminal CH3 beta to the O(+) and a =CH2; an RDKit substructure test of its pattern '[CH3][CH2][O+]=[CH2]' against this record's instantiated precursor returns NO match (the O(+)-alkyl chain here is propyl, not ethyl, and the oxocarbenium carbon carries an alkyl chain, not two hydrogens). (ii) DEFECT -- in IMS_8_11, IMS_8_13 and IMS_8_14_2 the expelled alkene is written on the right-hand side as '[C]1([H]2)([H]3)[C]5([H]6)([H]7)', i.e. a C-C SINGLE bond between two CH2 groups. That is not ethylene but a formal 1,2-biradical: the pi bond the mechanism forms is missing, so those rules conserve atoms/charge/spin (and therefore survive the conservation guardrail) while producing an under-bonded neutral. The correct product term is '[C]1([H]2)([H]3){=}[C]5([H]6)([H]7)'. Any future MØD rule for 8.94/8.95 must form that pi bond explicitly.
